newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity hits new highs on spot strength.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity hits new highs on spot strength.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading up Monday, hitting new contract highs on strength in the Western physical power market based on air conditioning demand in the Southwest, industry sources said.
"Our cash prices are up a little higher today from the weekend," said one Houston-based spot power and futures trader.

In the West, next day peak physical, firm Palo Verde (PV) was said to have traded at $22.00 and $23.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), while peak, firm next-day California Oregon Border (COB) was said to have traded at $16.75 and $17.00 per MWh, although the trades were unconfirmed.

Warm temperatures, forecast to reach near 100 degrees Fahrenheit in the Phoenix-Tuscson area of Arizona, were putting upward pressure on short-term physical power prices due to air conditioning demand, the sources said.
COB power prices for Northwest delivery were said to be rising in sympathy with Southwest values.

As of 1215 EDT, June Palo Verde (PV) had traded up 50 cents at $21.25 per megawatt hour (MWh) after hitting a new contract high of $21.45 and reaching as low as $20.70, while July was up 60 cents at the day's high of $25.20 after reaching as low as $24.60 per MWh.
Resistance in the PV June contracts was seen at $21.50 and $21.70 per MWh. "When we reach up to those levels there seems to be a lot of sellers jumping in the ring," said one trader.
June California Oregon Border (COB) was up 30 cents at $15.30 after hitting a new contract high of $15.50 per MWh, while July was up 15 cents at $16.95 from trades in a range of $16.85-16.95 per MWh.
NYMEX said that as of 1145 EDT an estimated total of 78 COB and 104 PV contracts had traded.
Market sources said a downturn in gas prices were having little impact on power futures.
As of 1220 EDT, June NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading down 2.2 cents at $2.245 per million British thermal units.

Weather Services Corp said in its latest six to 10 day outlook that temperatures in the Northwest would average well above normal with near normal precipitation, while readings in the Southwest would run above to well above normal with little or no precipitation.

Generation capacity in the western U.S. remained limited, with about 8,000 megawatts in the West said to be currently offline for repairs or maintenance, although much of the idled capacity was expected to return to service later this month.
COB open interest for May 2 rose 112 to 4,667, while PV open interest fell seven to 5,574, NYMEX said.
